description: USE + RED + Four Golden Signals for every component. Each row reads left to right: Traffic, Errors, Latency (percentiles), Saturation, Utilization. Panel titles are prefixed with the signal they answer.

panels.title: Applications — RED from traces (Tempo span-metrics, service graph, Kafka clients)

panels.description: [Traffic] Spans per second per service from Tempo's span-metrics generator. Counts every span kind, so it is work done, not only inbound requests.
panels.title: Traffic · Span rate by service

panels.description: [Errors] Share of spans with status ERROR. 0 = healthy. Chaos breaks in the consumer show up here.
panels.title: Errors · Error ratio by service

panels.description: [Latency] Real Prometheus histogram (traces_spanmetrics_latency_bucket), so quantiles aggregate correctly across instances.
panels.title: Latency · Span latency p50 / p99 by service

panels.description: [Latency] Per call edge from Tempo's service graph, measured by the caller: e.g. consumer → hbase-regionserver.
panels.title: Latency · Dependency latency p99 (client side)

panels.description: [Traffic / Errors] Requests and failed requests per call edge from the service graph.
panels.title: Traffic / Errors · Dependency request + failure rate

panels.description: [Saturation] How far the consumer is behind. Client-side max lag from the consumer's own Kafka client (OTel), and committed-offset lag from kafka-exporter when that job is deployed.
panels.title: Saturation · Consumer lag (records)

panels.description: [Latency] Client-observed broker round trips: producer request latency, consumer fetch and commit latency. Kafka clients only publish avg/max, not percentiles.
panels.title: Latency · Kafka client latency (avg / max)

panels.description: [Errors] Producer record errors and retries per second; consumer failed rebalances.
panels.title: Errors · Kafka client errors + retries

panels.description: [Saturation] Fraction of time the producer waited for buffer memory, and records' time queued in the accumulator before send.
panels.title: Saturation · Producer buffer pressure

panels.description: [Traffic] RequestsPerSec summed across API versions.
panels.title: Traffic · Requests/s by API

panels.description: [Errors] ErrorsPerSec excluding error=NONE (which is the success count), plus failed produce/fetch at the topic layer.
panels.title: Errors · Error responses/s by API and code

panels.description: [Latency] Broker-side end-to-end request time. Yammer decaying-reservoir percentiles inside the broker. FetchConsumer includes the consumer's long-poll wait (fetch.max.wait.ms), so a flat few hundred ms there is normal on an idle topic.
panels.title: Latency · Request latency p50 / p99 / p99.9 (TotalTimeMs)

panels.description: [Latency] Where Produce time goes: request queue (waiting for a handler = saturation), local (log append), remote (waiting for replicas/acks), response queue, send.
panels.title: Latency · Produce p99 by phase

panels.description: [Latency] Time to fsync a log segment to disk.
panels.title: Latency · Log flush latency

panels.description: [Traffic] Client bytes produced and fetched (excludes replication).
panels.title: Traffic · Bytes in / out

panels.description: [Utilization] 1 - idle% for the request handler pool and network processors. Sustained > 70% means the broker is running out of threads.
panels.title: Utilization · Handler + network thread utilization

panels.description: [Saturation] Requests waiting for a handler, responses waiting for a network thread, and requests parked in purgatory (acks=all produce, long-poll fetch). One parked Fetch per idle consumer is normal.
panels.title: Saturation · Request queue, response queue, purgatory

panels.description: [Errors / Saturation] Under-replicated, under-min-ISR and offline replicas. Anything above 0 is a problem.
panels.title: Errors / Saturation · Replication health

panels.description: [Traffic] Rate of the num_ops count of each operation histogram.
panels.title: Traffic · Operations/s by type

panels.description: [Errors] RPC exceptions by class (NotServingRegion, RegionTooBusy, callTimedOut, ...) and operations over the slow-log threshold.
panels.title: Errors · RPC exceptions + slow operations

panels.description: [Latency] Server-side Get/Put/Scan/Increment latency in whole ms (decaying reservoir in the RegionServer).
panels.title: Latency · Operation latency p50 / p99 / max

panels.description: [Latency] putTime/getTime/scanTime/incrementTime p99 per table in the default namespace.
panels.title: Latency · Per-table latency p99

panels.description: [Latency / Saturation] QueueCallTime is time waiting for a handler thread (saturation); ProcessCallTime is the work itself.
panels.title: Latency / Saturation · RPC call time p99: queue vs processing

panels.description: [Latency] WAL sync/append and the RegionServer's HDFS reads/writes. WAL SyncTime is the write-path floor.
panels.title: Latency · WAL + HDFS IO latency p99

panels.description: [Saturation] Calls queued for handlers, active handlers, and background flush/compaction backlog. blockedRequestCount rising means writes are being blocked on memstore.
panels.title: Saturation · Handler, call queue, flush/compaction queues

panels.description: [Utilization] Active handlers as a share of hbase.regionserver.handler.count (default 30), block cache used share, and block cache hit ratio.
panels.title: Utilization · Handler, memstore, block cache utilization

panels.description: [Utilization] Data waiting to be flushed to HFiles.
panels.title: Utilization · Memstore size

panels.description: [Traffic / Latency] Master RPCs (region assignment, reports, DDL).
panels.title: Traffic / Latency · RPC call rate + p99

panels.description: [Errors] Region assignment operation failures and Master RPC exceptions.
panels.title: Errors · Assignment failures + RPC exceptions

panels.description: [Saturation] Regions stuck moving between servers. ritCountOverThreshold > 0 means stuck regions.
panels.title: Saturation · Regions in transition

panels.description: [Traffic] Client and DataNode protocol calls per method (RpcDetailedActivity).
panels.title: Traffic · RPC calls/s by method

panels.description: [Errors] Exceptions thrown back to clients by class, calls flagged slow, and missing/corrupt blocks and dead DataNodes.
panels.title: Errors · RPC exceptions, slow calls, block errors

panels.description: [Latency] rpcQueueTime / rpcProcessingTime 60 s rolling percentiles, enabled by rpc.metrics.quantile.enable in hdfs-site.xml. Queue time = waiting for a handler.
panels.title: Latency · RPC latency percentiles (queue / processing)

panels.description: [Latency] Time to fsync the edit log (every namespace write waits on this). From dfs.metrics.percentiles.intervals.
panels.title: Latency · Edit-log sync latency

panels.description: [Saturation] RPC call queue depth, threads waiting on the namesystem lock, and RPC lock wait p99.
panels.title: Saturation · Call queue, lock queue, lock wait

panels.description: [Utilization] DFS capacity used as a share of total cluster capacity.
panels.title: Utilization · Capacity used

panels.description: [Saturation] Blocks waiting for re-replication or deletion, and files still open for write. Growing backlog = NameNode or DataNodes can't keep up.
panels.title: Saturation · Replication + deletion backlog

panels.description: [Traffic] Bytes read/written and block read/write operations per second.
panels.title: Traffic · Bytes + block ops

panels.description: [Errors] DataNode network errors, file-IO errors per volume, block verification failures, failed volumes.
panels.title: Errors · Network, IO and volume errors

panels.description: [Latency] PacketAckRoundTripTimeNanos = write latency as the HDFS client sees it; FlushNanos/FsyncNanos = local disk. Nanoseconds.
panels.title: Latency · Write pipeline latency p99

panels.description: [Latency] Per-volume file IO latency (dfs.datanode.fileio.profiling.sampling.percentage). Whole ms; sub-ms IO reads 0.
panels.title: Latency · Volume IO latency p99

panels.description: [Saturation] Active DataXceiver threads (one per block read/write stream). The limit is dfs.datanode.max.transfer.threads (default 4096).
panels.title: Saturation · Xceivers + transfer threads

panels.description: [Utilization] DFS used share of the DataNode's configured capacity.
panels.title: Utilization · Disk used
JVMs — USE per process (JMX exporter + OTel agent)

panels.description: [Utilization] Process CPU of each JVM in cores (JMX exporter's process collector).
panels.title: Utilization · CPU (cores)

panels.description: [Utilization] Heap used / heap max for broker and Hadoop/HBase JVMs.
panels.title: Utilization · Heap used share

panels.description: [Saturation] Fraction of wall time spent in GC. > 5% sustained means heap pressure.
panels.title: Saturation · Time in GC

panels.description: [Utilization] Recent CPU utilization reported by the OTel Java agent, which runs in every JVM here: the apps plus Kafka, ZooKeeper, HBase and HDFS. Share of all host cores.
panels.title: Utilization · JVM CPU utilization (OTel agent)

panels.description: [Saturation / Errors] Threads blocked on monitors and any deadlock (should always be 0).
panels.title: Saturation / Errors · Blocked + deadlocked threads

panels.description: [Errors] ERROR/FATAL log lines per second from the Hadoop JvmMetrics log counters.
panels.title: Errors · Logged errors (Hadoop/HBase log4j)

panels.description: [Utilization] CPU used per container, in cores.
panels.title: Utilization · CPU (cores)

panels.description: [Saturation] Share of time at least one task in the container was runnable but waiting for CPU (Linux pressure-stall information). The direct CPU saturation signal.
panels.title: Saturation · CPU pressure (PSI waiting)

panels.description: [Utilization] Working-set memory per container (what the OOM killer looks at).
panels.title: Utilization · Memory working set

panels.description: [Saturation] Share of time tasks waited on memory reclaim or block IO.
panels.title: Saturation · Memory + IO pressure (PSI waiting)

panels.description: [Utilization] Block-device read+write bytes and network receive+transmit bytes per container.
panels.title: Utilization · Disk + network throughput

panels.description: [Errors] OOM events and network interface errors or dropped packets per container.

targets.expr: sum by (service) (rate(container_network_receive_errors_total{job="cadvisor", service!=""}[$__rate_interval]) + rate(container_network_transmit_errors_total{job="cadvisor", service!=""}[$__rate_interval]) + rate(container_network_receive_packets_dropped_total{job="cadvisor", service!=""}[$__rate_interval]) + rate(container_network_transmit_packets_dropped_total{job="cadvisor", service!=""}[$__rate_interval])) > 0

panels.title: Errors · OOM kills + network errors/drops

title: OTel Lab — Golden Signals (USE + RED)
